full_judgment: 7. On appeal by the defendant No. 1 the appellate Court reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court on the finding that the suit as framed was not maintainable since the evidence on record shows that the defendants are in possession of the land in suit and, as such, plaintiffs were required to seek declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. The appellate Court also observed that trial Court was in error in decreeing the suit in part i.e. decreeing the suit in favour of the plaintiff Nos. 2-4. The appellate Court further held that the document on the basis of which plaintiff Nos. 2-4 were claiming the land in suit is not genuine since the signature of the executants of the kabala and the signature of the identifier of the said kabala is of the same hand. It was also noticed by the appellate Court that the PWs 2 and 3 admitted possession of the land in suit by the defendants. It may be mentioned it was the contention of the appellant that the suit framed is not maintainable since the land in suit is unspecified and description of the land claimed by the plaintiffs is vague, in that there is no statement that plaintiffs are in possession of which part of the land of the suit plots as mentioned in schedule 'Ga'. The appellate Court upon allowing the appeal set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and thereupon dismissed the suit.
